newsitem.title: USA: U.S. asks Sandinistas to withdraw campaign ad.
newsitem.headline: U.S. asks Sandinistas to withdraw campaign ad.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it had asked the Sandinista Front of former Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega to withdraw a televised election advertisement showing him next to a U.S. congressman.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the advertisement showing Ortega and Representative Bill Richardson, Democrat of New Mexico, gave a misleading impression that the left-wing Ortega was close to the United States.
Burns told reporters that Richardson, who is close to the Clinton administration and sometimes acts as an unofficial envoy abroad, had been a "target of opportunity".
"Richardson visits Nicaragua and Ortega comes up at some event, stands next to him, they film them together, (and) Ortega says 'I'm a friend of the United States'," Burns said.
"We have protested the use of this video to Ortega's political party," he said. "We have asked for an immediate withdrawal of the televised advertisement."

"This involves an elected member of the United States Congress and we are simply doing what we can to see that the campaign does not contain information or lend an appearance that is inacurate about an American connection with Mr. Ortega."
Burns said the State Department had discussed its move with Richardson, but did not say whether the congressman planned to protest himself.
Ortega, who was unexpectedly defeated in 1990 elections by Violeta Chamorro, is standing this month against Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance.
Ortega was high on the list of U.S. public enemies during the 1980s, when Washington supported guerrillas against his government in Nicaragua.

Burns said on Tuesday he stood by public remarks he made last Friday, when he said that he "would not use the word democrat to describe Daniel Ortega", and that Washington remembered Ortega's past actions against the United States.
